Tail-heavy guide

This guide has a valuable opening and a deliberately long sequence of supporting sections. The complete source remains available, but an agent with a small context budget may request a bounded core. OmniRead must shape that response only after full extraction and verification.

Core decision

Coverage describes the requested response envelope. Full means no deliberate budget bound. Core means a section-boundary prefix was returned and every omitted anchor is named. Neither label changes whether the source capture itself was truthful.

Evidence model

The verifier compares visible headings, DOM words, publisher declarations, block signals, and pagination. It runs against the full extracted source before token shaping. A bounded core can therefore retain a complete verdict without pretending the response contains every section.

Implementation notes

Token estimates come from the same outline used for section selection. Remaining item count is the number of omitted sections, and extra tokens are the sum of those sections. No percentage or confidence score is invented.

Operational examples

The command line accepts a budget for the core response and a full flag for escalation. MCP returns a handle that can retrieve one section or request the full result. Both adapters expose the identical typed object.

Long tail

Supporting examples, edge cases, and repeated discussion may be useful later but need not consume the first context window. Their omission is declared, priced, and reversible. This is useful compression rather than silent loss.

Closing checklist

Verify the source first. Bound only at section boundaries. Name every omitted anchor. Report the remaining count and token estimate. Preserve the independent completeness verdict. Escalate explicitly when the agent decides the tail is worth its cost.
